question: To gain better insight as to how the HD cells behaved in the symmetric scene, the tuning of the individual HD neurons was plotted for the pre-learning, learning and post-learning epochs, after centring to and sorting by the preferred orientation b.

analyse_plan.Objective: Characterize how the tuning curves of individual HD cells change across the pre-learning, learning and post-learning epochs in the symmetry experiment by plotting epoch-wise tuning maps after centring to and sorting by the preferred orientation b.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Verify that HD cells are identified using one-half of the pre-learning epoch data. Verify that the tuning curves are calculated from average fluorescence binned according to the centred scene orientation θ − b. Confirm that the tuning curves are centred to and sorted by the preferred orientation b before rendering the three epoch-wise tuning maps.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1.Load Data: Load the fluorescence traces and scene-orientation traces from the symmetry experiment.2. Identify HD Cells: Identify HD cells using the reported sinusoidal fitting procedure on one-half of the pre-learning epoch data.3.Compute Tuning Curves: Calculate the average fluorescence of each selected HD cell binned according to the centred scene orientation θ − b for the pre-learning, learning and post-learning epochs.4.Centre and Sort: Centre each tuning curve to the preferred orientation b and sort the ROIs by b. 5.Save Key Results: Save the centred tuning matrices and ROI ordering for downstream checking and reuse. 6.Visualization: Render the epoch-wise tuning maps with a shared colour scale.

key_analysis_results: During the learning epoch of the symmetry experiment, the tuning of the HD cells appeared bimodal, and the tuning in the symmetric scene appeared not simply doubled, but also rotated in a systematic way according to their preferred scene orientation.
key_analysis_conclusions: In the symmetric scene, the tuning of the HD cells appeared not simply doubled, but also rotated in a systematic way according to their preferred scene orientation.

summary_report.abstract: To gain better insight as to how the HD cells behaved in the symmetric scene, the tuning curves of individual HD cells were plotted for the pre-learning, learning and post-learning epochs after centring to and sorting by the preferred orientation b, showing that although the tuning of the HD cells during the learning epoch appeared bimodal, the tuning in the symmetric scene appeared not simply doubled, but also rotated in a systematic way according to their preferred scene orientation.
summary_report.methods: The tuning of individual HD neurons was examined across the pre-learning, learning and post-learning epochs in the symmetry experiment. For each selected HD ROI, the average fluorescence was calculated binned according to the centred scene orientation θ − b, where b is the preferred scene orientation of the ROI. HD cells were identified with the reported sinusoidal fitting procedure using one-half of the pre-learning epoch data, and the epoch-wise tuning curves were then centred to and sorted by the preferred orientation b for visualization.
summary_report.results: The epoch-wise tuning maps showed that the tuning of the HD cells during the learning epoch appeared bimodal. At the same time, the tuning in the symmetric scene appeared not simply doubled, but also rotated in a systematic way according to preferred scene orientation, so the pattern across the HD-cell population was not a simple duplicated version of the single-sun tuning profile.
summary_report.discussion: These tuning maps indicate that the effect of the symmetric scene on HD-cell tuning cannot be explained by simple twofold duplication alone. Instead, the changes in tuning depend on preferred scene orientation and are consistent with a systematic rotation of tuning across the HD-cell population in the symmetric scene.
